newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zairean rebels urge Swiss to freeze Mobutu wealth.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels urge Swiss to freeze Mobutu wealth.

text.p: Zairean rebels urged Swiss authorities on Tuesday to freeze any wealth that embattled President Mobuto Sese Seko may have on deposit in Switzerland and said they were seeking legal assistance from Berne in the case.

Edi Angulu, European spokesman for the AFDL rebel alliance, told reporters the group had sent the request to Berne on March 4 outlining their accusations that Mobutu had amassed a fortune in public funds and stashed it in Switzerland, the Swiss SDA news agency reported.

But a Swiss foreign ministry spokesman said he was unaware of such a petition and added the rebels had no basis to act because only governments could ask for international legal assistance from authorities in another country.
"There can be no request for legal assistance because this a possibility only open to governments," Livio Zanolari told Reuters from Berne.
Zaire's rebel leader, Laurent Kabila, has already demanded the repatriation of Mobutu's fortune, and some Swiss members of parliament have backed the idea.
The 66-year-old Zairean ruler returned home only this month to face the rebellion in the east after undergoing prostate cancer surgery in Switzerland last August and convalescing there and in France.
Mobutu's holdings in Switzerland are widely estimated by Swiss media at around $4 billion, but the Swiss Bankers Association has said it has no reason to believe this is so.
